territorial_scope.description: Applies to any person with respect to federal elections in the United States; the text states no reach beyond that.

evidence.quote: No person, whether acting under color of law or otherwise, shall use an artificial intelligence system

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends federal law to prohibit materially false information about time, place, manner or voter eligibility for federal elections, including AI-generated content, within 60 days before those elections, and voter intimidation or hindrance. Adds a private civil action, criminal penalties including up to 1 year's imprisonment, and Attorney General corrective communications.
summary.long: The bill, the Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025, amends the Revised Statutes (52 U.S.C. 10101) and Title 18 of the United States Code. Section 3 prohibits any person, whether acting under color of law or otherwise, from communicating or producing materially false information about the time, place or manner of federal elections, or about voter eligibility or registration status, within 60 days before such an election, with intent to impede voting. A separate provision bars using an artificial intelligence system, including a generative system, to produce such information with intent to use it for that purpose. Intentionally hindering or interfering with voting, including by operating a falsely labelled polling place, is also prohibited. Violations of the criminal provisions carry a fine or imprisonment for not more than 1 year, or both. A person aggrieved by a violation may bring a civil action for preventive relief, and the court may award attorney's fees. Section 4 directs the Attorney General, after a credible report and where state and local officials have not corrected the information, to communicate accurate corrective information, and to publish procedures within 180 days of enactment. Section 3 also directs the Sentencing Commission to review sentencing guidelines within 180 days and amends the Voting Rights Act to cover payments for not voting. Section 5 requires reports to Congress after each federal general election, made public. Section 6 gives election officials a civil action, and Section 7 makes intimidation of ballot tabulation, canvass and certification efforts a crime under the National Voter Registration Act. The bill is at the introduction stage.

notes: Bill as introduced; no enacted text, so no consolidated version exists. Relations to instruments outside the registry carry an empty target_instrument_id. Citation inconsistency: Sec. 3(b)(1) amends 52 U.S.C. 10101(c), but Sec. 6 refers to the same subsection (c)(2) as 52 U.S.C. 10101(b). Election definitions differ: new 52 U.S.C. 10101(b)(4) (Sec. 3(a)) lists Presidential elector, Member of the Senate and Territory or possession, while new 18 U.S.C. 594(d) (Sec. 3(c)(1)(C)) lists Senator and Resident Commissioner to the Congress and omits Presidential elector. The generative AI prohibition (new 52 U.S.C. 10101(b)(2)(B)) requires intent to produce false information, not knowledge of material falsity as in (b)(2)(A). Sec. 2 findings cite a 2025 appellate ruling and constitutional bases; they are context, not operative provisions. Deadlines run from the date of enactment; no calendar date is stated.
